text:
ellen: FYI — noticed a spike in mobile-txrecompute for us-west this morning. several tenants' dashboard freshness jumped from <30m to ~4h, and the recompute workers report many high-cardinality windows (user_id sharding) causing long tail.

raj: any idea what's different vs normal? more late events or hitter partitioning?

ellen: looks like a late batch from the mobile ingestion pipeline; manifests arrived late and a few of the windows include thousands of unique ids. workload profile: many small windows but extremely high unique-key counts.

priya: that pattern kills continuous-replay. two paths: 1) route to the "cardinality-special" pool with more memory and wider join sketching, 2) fall back to approximate-count sketches (HyperLogLog) for the dashboard panels.

zach: prefer path 1 for billing-critical tenants, but path 2 could be fine for non-billing dashboards. we need a per-tenant policy.

ellen: agreed. console needs a per-tenant flag: recompute_policy = [exact, best-effort, approximate]. default is exact. owners can set override.

raj: API debate: do we surface recompute_policy at the routing layer or at the job submission API? If exposed at routing, internal services can make decisions without asking the console. If at submission, console has to pass it each time.

priya: I vote routing layer. routing-eval can look up tenant policy and tags. also easier to apply emergency overrides (feature flags) without changing clients.

zach: downside: routing layer becomes another source of truth duplication with console. need a small cache invalidation story.

ellen: implementation sketch: store policy in config-store (per-tenant row). routing-eval fetches and caches for 30s. console writes update to config-store and emits a config-change event. sounds reasonable?

raj: also suggest a soft budget per-tenant for fast-pool minutes. token accounting: each fast-pool run consumes tokens proportional to estimated-unique-keys * window_minutes / 1000. token-balance can be viewed in the console and admins can top-up.

priya: operational rule: if estimated_unique_keys > 500k or estimated_memory > 8GB => reject fast-pool and route to batch-pool unless tenant policy == exact and admin override present. we shouldn't OOM the fast-pool.

zach: good. what about the approximate path? we need a schema indicator in the telemetry API response so downstream consumers know the value may be sketch-based. add fields `approx_method` and `approx_error_bound`.

ellen: agree. also require the console to show an "approx warning" banner when tiles are using sketch-based values for >5% of their datapoints in the last 24h.

raj: small proto for routing-eval call:
```
POST /internal/routing-eval
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "shard": "mobile-agg-7",
  "window_minutes": 15,
  "est_unique_keys": 210000
}
// response: route: "fast-pool", allowed_variant: ["exact"], reason: "policy=best-effort, tokens_ok"
```

priya: testing note: add property-based tests that fuzz est_unique_keys and assert the policy decision boundaries. we'll also simulate a mem-pressure event and ensure fast-pool evicts lowest-priority tenants first.

zach: metrics to add: per-tenant fast-pool token consumption, percent of tiles showing sketch values, number of rejects due to high-cardinality. Dash-team wants an alert when >2% of tenant tiles shift to approximate in a 30m window.

deploy-bot: Canary config updated: fast-pool-token-bucket enabled for 5% of tenants. :rocket:

ellen: timeline proposal: config-store + routing-eval change this week, console flag and UI indicators next week, sketches implementation and telemetry in two weeks. we can run canary and measure downstream delta for a small tenant cohort.

raj: I'll draft the runbook for rollback: how to detect sketch-tile regressions, how to re-run exact recompute on batch-pool, and how to force-disable approximate variants per-tenant via emergency flag.

priya: I'll add the property tests and the mem-pressure simulation. zach can pair on quota accounting logic.

zach: happy to. I'll also add a console mockup for the policy selector and the token balance widget.

ellen: thanks. ticket created: REPRO-514 (high-cardinality routing + sketch fallback). pinging @dash-team and @billing for awareness.

priya: minor ask: ensure billing doesn't use sketch values for invoiceable metrics unless tenant opted in. we'll gate that in the billing pipeline by checking telemetry.approx_method==null.

ellen: noted. good catch.

zach: ok lets sync tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:
